facts.says: Share of Hawaiʻi residents' net long-term capital gains reported by filers with Hawaiʻi AGI of $400,000 or more
facts.source: Hawaiʻi Department of Taxation, Hawaiʻi Individual Income Tax Statistics, Tax Year 2023, Table 21
facts.checked: Claude against the TY2023 XLSX ($2,041.4M of $2,645.7M, residents), 2026-11-23
facts.note: Residents and nonresidents together in TY2023 are also 77 percent.

history.note: TY2022 Table 21, residents and nonresidents together ($3,110.6M of $4,420.9M).

facts.says: Hawaiʻi's top individual income tax rate
facts.source: Act 24, SLH 2026 (SB 3125); brackets as presented by the Department of Taxation to the Tax Review Commission, May 2026
facts.match: top (income tax )?rate|wages are taxed up to|income from wages|taxed up to
facts.checked: Claude against the DOTAX presentation, slides 12-15, 2026-11-23 (the Act text itself was not opened)
facts.note: 13 percent applies above $500,000 of taxable income for single and married-filing-separately filers, $750,000 for heads of household and $1,000,000 for joint filers. The act is Act 24, not Act 25.

history.note: Pin words about 2026 law to a 2026 date and they keep saying 11 percent.

facts.says: Number of Hawaiʻi residents with $1 million or more in net wealth
facts.source: Altrata (formerly Wealth-X), Market Sizing Wealth Data for Hawaiʻi, November 9, 2025
facts.checked: Claude against the Altrata export, $1m+ row, 2026-11-23
facts.note: Altrata's tiers are cumulative ($1m+ includes $20m+ and $50m+). 83,059 and 83,424 were double-counted totals from older dashboard versions.

facts.says: State EITC that working families would lose in tax year 2028 if the Act 163 expansions lapse
facts.source: Hawaiʻi Appleseed microsimulation of the working family credits (90 percent range $41.1 million to $42.3 million)
facts.match: earned income tax credit loss|from the (state )?(earned income tax credit|EITC)|EITC loss
facts.note: The same run gives $33.8 million from the food/excise credit and $84.6 million in all. wfc-credits' Table 8 (42.8) and the fact sheet's $43M come from an earlier run.
